title: Pricing/packaging scratchpad — token math & tier ideas
body:
Goal: quick back-of-envelope for token unit costs and a few tier ideas. Not final - lots of assumptions listed.

ASSUMPTIONS (rough)
- Target model family for pricing baseline: 20B transformer (quantized variant for production).
- Throughput per GPU (p99-ish batch pipeline): 50 tokens/sec average across mixed workloads (varies a lot).
- GPU cost (amortized infra + cloud + misc) per hour: $3.50 (includes kernels, infra, network, admin amortization).
- Average request overhead + CPU + storage amortized = $0.50/hr-equivalent per GPU.
- Total effective cost per GPU-hour: $4.00.
- Tokens per hour per GPU = 50 * 3600 = 180k tokens/hr.

BASE COST PER TOKEN
- Cost per token = $4.00 / 180,000 = $0.0000222 (~2.2e-05) per token.
- Round: ~0.000022 ($0.022 per 1k tokens).

OTHER FACTORS / ADJUSTMENTS
- Batching & KV cache: optimizations could improve tokens/sec by 2x for steady-state workloads -> cost/token ~0.000011.
- Short prompt overhead: cold KV + context loading increases per-request cost; per-request fixed CPU = ~0.5-2 cents depending on latency tier; for many tiny requests that dominates.
- Embeddings and smaller models: cost/token lower; we should treat embeddings separately (different stack).
- Multi-tenant vs dedicated: dedicated reserved capacity amortization reduces cost per token for big customers (committed discounts).

PRICE SUGGESTIONS (hosted API, simple tiers)
Notes: margin target 60%+ on hosted API; cover SRE, R&D, support, sales.
- Free tier: 100k tokens/mo free (developer trials).
- Developer (pay-as-you-go): $0.00006 per token -> margin ~73% vs base 0.000022
  - Implied price per 1K tokens = $0.06
- Team: $0.000045 per token -> price per 1K = $0.045 (bulk discount for regular usage)
  - Margin ~51% vs base
- Business / SLA (includes priority, 99.9 SLA): $0.00012 per token -> $0.12 per 1K (higher because reserved capacity + support)
- Committed / Dedicated: negotiated, example: $0.00001-0.000015 per token equivalent when big commit + year-term (close to infra marginal cost with reserved hardware)

Quick check: if we price dev @ $0.00006, revenue per token - cost = 0.0000378 -> for 1M tokens rev = $60, cost = $22.2, gross = $37.8. Reasonable for hosted API.

Tier ideas (feature + pricing mapping)
- Free: 100k tokens, community support, model catalog limited to smaller/older models.
- Developer: pay-as-you-go, streaming, function-calls, no SLA, some rate limits. (good for PLG)
- Team: monthly plan with included tokens (e.g., 5M tokens/mo) + discounted overage; shared keys, basic audit logs.
- Business: higher included tokens, higher throughput rate limits, priority support, longer retention in Console, SLA.
- Dedicated/Private: quoting (reserved GPU capacity), charged by GPU-hour + optional platform fee; include baseline pricing formula: base GPU-hour * reserved hours + data plane egress + support.

Unit economics per user example
- Small startup: 5M tokens/mo on Team plan priced at $0.045/1K = $225/mo revenue. Cost = 5,000 * 0.0222 = $111 -> gross margin ~$114 (51%).
- High volume AI app: 1B tokens/mo on committed discount $0.000012/token -> rev = $12,000, cost = 1,000,000 * 0.0222 = $22,200 -> wait that math mismatch: need consistent units. Recompute: 1B tokens -> cost = 1,000,000,000 * 0.0000222 = $22,200. Rev at $0.000012/token = $12,000 -> negative margin. So committed price must be >= cost.
  - To be profitable, committed price should be >= cost per token (0.000022) unless there's other savings (e.g., better reserved infra cost 50% lower). If reserved infra halves cost -> cost/token ~0.000011 -> then pricing at $0.000012 yields small margin.

Open questions / uncertainties
- GPU cost estimates are fuzzy: need infra team for realistic fleet amortization, networking, failed jobs, multi-tenant overhead.
- Throughput numbers depend heavily on model, input lengths, and caching. Need per-model profiles.
- How to handle short-chat dominated workloads (many small requests): best to build per-request fee + per-token to avoid margin erosion.
- Embeddings pricing model should be separate (often sold per 1k embeddings or per vector).
- Should we include a per-request "compute overhead" fee for sub-512-token requests? Consider e.g., $0.002 per request as a floor.

Action items / next steps
- Ask infra for 1) realistic cost per GPU-hour including reserved vs spot; 2) typical throughput by model family (tokens/sec) for our runtime. (owner: Samir)
- Pull 90-day usage histogram from hosted API (tokens per request distribution) to quantify tiny-request problem (owner: Aileen).
- Prototype alternative pricing: hybrid model with request-floor + per-token for 3 months on a subset of users to measure churn/elasticity.
- Draft public pricing page copy + sample invoices for top 3 personas.

Notes to self: sticky points are short-request workloads and committed discounts. We should not underprice committed/dedicated deals unless we can guarantee hardware amortization or sell add-on platform fees.

Rough conclusion: baseline break-even token cost ~0.000022. Dev paid price ~0.00006 looks safe. Committed pricing must be tied to capacity commitments (hours/GPU) or risk negative margins.

-- jordan
